items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: And in 1923 he came back again. And I used to let him sit in with me and play in the band.

ctx.x: You've told about that on the tape.
Yeah, it was just about to finish. And he left the high school and came up there. And in 1923 he came back again. And I used to let him sit in with me and play in the band.
And then sit down. You'd actually sit there and play?

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: Asked me to show him different things, which I did.

ctx.x: And he had some very nice things to say about you and talked about your playing. So you'll be happy to know that other people are backing your story up. If you go to the musicians, some of them will. And Raymond is one of them who will back you up.

Well, Sharky might because Sharky got up and Sharky lost his place in the jazz club by telling the people I was the one who brought this music around the world. Sharky was pulled off a program for the same thing. Now, Sharky was born about eight, nine years old when I was a musician playing music. Sharky wasn't playing music. Harry Shields wasn't playing music. Parenti wasn't playing music. George's Brunessons that they played. They weren't around. But they all got their mouth open big as an alligator trying to…
Now, I know you or I, we don't want to take credit away from Bix for what he had. Bix is a great man. Yes.
